CLASSIFICATION COMPLETE. The vignette reviewer worked the Class I / Class II split term by term against what each constructor actually enforces. Result:

  CLASS II - load-bearing, must be TAUGHT, never renamed or defaulted away.  SIX terms:
    measurement frame          one sparse object covering voxel/searchlight/ROI/whole-brain.
                               'ROI definition' and 'searchlight scheme' each cover one case;
                               the unification is the central claim and has no standard name.
    coherent / configuration   vision.md:114 explicitly refuses 'univariate/multivariate' and
                               is right to: those come from separately fitted pipelines,
                               whereas total = coherent + configuration is an EXACT additive
                               split. Standard terms cannot express that.
    effect form (asymmetric)   no standard name for 'bilinear form whose two axes carry
                               independent named bases'.
    pairing                    genuinely not a cross-validation scheme - not train/test, but
                               which ordered partition products enter the estimate. Per
                               vision.md:116 the choice changes the estimand.
    oriented                   narrow, but the sign-survival argument is real.
    Parseval frame / canonical dual   precise frame-theory terms, correctly used.

  CLASS I - existing idea renamed, safe to rename to the field's word.  ~13 terms:
    relation -> dataset/pattern matrices,  partition -> run/session/block,
    effect space -> conditions,  measurement space -> common space,  leg -> projection,
    native -> voxel-level,  capability -> requirement/precondition,
    construction claim -> assumption,  geometry -> representational geometry / second-moment G

  CLASS I-d - a sub-case I had not anticipated and the reviewer added. Implementation
  vocabulary with NO scientific content, which should not be renamed but DELETED from user
  docs entirely:
    tomography       README.md:219. Not a concept at all - it is the internal filename
                     R/tomography.R, exported nowhere, leaked into the README.
    lowering, contraction, materialize, packed, support-local, support-streamed,
    feature atoms, query-first

MY PROVISIONAL LIST WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND I AM RECORDING BOTH ERRORS.

  I put 'capability gating' in Class II. The reviewer puts the WORD in Class I - the
  permissions table at evidence-pairing.Rmd:445-453 is genuinely valuable content, but the
  word 'capability' adds nothing to it that 'requirement' would not. The GUARANTEE is Class
  II; the VOCABULARY is Class I. I had conflated them. That distinction generalises: in every
  Class I case the reviewer checked, the guarantee lives in the constructor's argument
  validation, not in the noun. Renaming the noun cannot destroy it.

  I omitted 'measurement frame' entirely, and it is the single strongest Class II term in
  the package.

  I had not conceived of Class I-d.

THE NUMBER IS THE FINDING: 6 versus ~19. The danger I raised in this bead is real but far
narrower than I framed it. Six is a teachable number. Twenty-five is not. Flattening the
Class I set and deleting the Class I-d set destroys nothing and is most of the perceived
difficulty of this package.

Still wanted from claude-review: promote anything from Class I to Class II that you believe
the constructor does NOT independently enforce. That is now the only remaining question on
this bead, and it is a narrow one.
